entries.title: Proverbs 27:1
segments: Do not boast yourself of tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring forth.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:2
segments: Let another man praise you, and not your mouth; a stranger, and not your lips.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:3
segments: A stone [is] heavy, and sand [is] heavy; but a fool's wrath [is] heavier than them both.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:4
segments: Wrath [is] cruel, and anger [is] overwhelming; but who [is] able to stand before envy?

entries.title: Proverbs 27:5
segments: Open rebuke [is] better than secret love.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:6
segments: Faithful [are] the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy [are] deceitful.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:7
segments: The full soul despises a honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing [is] sweet.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:8
segments: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so [is] a man who wanders from his place.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:9
segments: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart; so does the sweetness of one's friend by advice from the heart.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:10
segments: Your own friend, and your father's friend, do not forsake them; nor go to your brother's house in the day of your trouble; better [is] a neighbor that is near than a brother far off.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:11
segments: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, so that I may answer him who shames me.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:12
segments: A sensible one foresees the evil [and] hides himself, but the simple pass on [and] are punished.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:13
segments: Take his robe that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge from him for a strange woman.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:14
segments: He who blesses his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:15
segments: A never-ending dropping in a very rainy day and a quarrelsome woman are alike.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:16
segments: Whoever hides her hides the wind, and his right [hand] encounters [slippery] oil.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:17
segments: Iron sharpens iron, so a man sharpens the face of his friend.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:18
segments: Whoever keeps the fig tree shall eat its fruit; so he who waits on his master shall be honored.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:19
segments: As in water face [answers] to face, so the heart of man [answers] to man.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:20
segments: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:21
segments: [As] the refining pot for silver and the furnace for gold, so [is] a man to his praise.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:22
segments: Though you should pound a fool in a bowl with a bar in the midst of wheat, his foolishness will not depart from him.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:23
segments: Know well the face of your flocks; set your heart on your herds.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:24
segments: For riches [are] not forever; nor the crown from generation to generation?

entries.title: Proverbs 27:25
segments: When the hay is removed, and the tender grass is seen, and mountain-plants are gathered,

entries.title: Proverbs 27:26
segments: the lambs [are] for your clothing, and the goats [are] the price of the field.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:27
segments: And [you shall have] goats' milk enough for your food, for the food of your household, and a living for your young women.
